extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers, journal editors, and researchers in health and biomedical research seeking reporting checklists and guidance
extracted.subtask_description: A searchable library/catalog of reporting guidelines for health research that lists dozens–hundreds of checklist-style and narrative guidance documents (e.g., CONSORT, PRISMA, STROBE, SPIRIT, STARD, TRIPOD, CARE, ARRIVE, SQUIRE, CHEERS and many extensions). Used to find the appropriate reporting standard for a given study design or specialty.

rubrics_metrics.name: EQUATOR Library (catalog of reporting guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: A comprehensive library/index that lists reporting guidelines (most recently added displayed first) for many study designs, specialties and methods in health research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts as a central catalogue to find reporting checklists and guidance documents. The Library includes items for randomized trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, diagnostic/prognostic studies, protocols, case reports, qualitative research, animal studies, quality improvement studies, economic evaluations, and many specialty and methodological extensions. Use it to identify the appropriate guideline for your study type or field.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is a reporting guideline?
rubrics_metrics.description: A reporting guideline is a checklist, flow diagram, or explicit text to guide authors when reporting health research, to improve transparency and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting guidelines typically list essential items to include in manuscripts (methods, results, context, limitations, etc.). The Library links to guideline statements, checklists, and explanations/elaborations where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT (randomised trials) and CONSORT Extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred items for reporting randomized trials (CONSORT 2010 and multiple extensions for specific trial designs and contexts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CONSORT provides a checklist and flow diagram covering trial design, participants, interventions, outcomes, sample size, randomization, blinding, statistical methods, and harms; many extensions tailor items for cluster trials, adaptive designs, N-of-1, non-pharmacologic treatments, device trials, etc. Use the specific CONSORT extension matching the trial design.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA (systematic reviews and meta-analyses) and PRISMA Extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) and multiple extensions (e.g., PRISMA-ScR, PRISMA-DTA, PRISMA for abstracts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRISMA checklists cover title, abstract, rationale, objectives, eligibility criteria, information sources, search strategy, study selection, data collection, risk of bias, synthesis methods, results, discussion, and registration. Select the PRISMA extension appropriate for review type (scoping, diagnostic accuracy, living reviews, abstracts, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE (observational studies) and STROBE Extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) statement and extensions for specific observational designs and subfields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STROBE checklists include items on study design, setting, participants, variables, data sources/measurement, bias, study size, quantitative variables, statistical methods, results, limitations, interpretation, and generalizability. Use extensions (e.g., STROBE-MR, STROBE-Vet) when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPIRIT (clinical trial protocols) and SPIRIT Extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard protocol items for clinical trials (SPIRIT) that define the minimum content of trial protocols; extensions available for specific contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPIRIT specifies required protocol elements such as background, objectives, trial design, eligibility, interventions, outcomes, sample size, allocation, blinding, data collection and management, statistical methods, oversight committees, and dissemination plans. Use SPIRIT extensions (e.g., SPIRIT-AI, SPIRIT-TCM) for specialized interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD (diagnostic accuracy studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for Reporting Diagnostic accuracy studies (STARD) defining essential items for reporting studies that evaluate diagnostic tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STARD items include information on the index test, reference standard, participant selection, test procedures, blinding, statistical analyses, and flow of participants. Extensions such as STARD for abstracts exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPOD (prediction model studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis Or Diagnosis (TRIPOD) guidance for development and validation of prediction models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TRIPOD covers title/abstract, background, source of data, participants, outcome definition, predictors, sample size, missing data, statistical methods, model performance measures, and discussion of limitations and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: CARE (case reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: CAse REport (CARE) guidelines defining recommended items to include in clinical case reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CARE checklist addresses title, keywords, abstract, introduction, patient information, clinical findings, timeline, diagnostic assessment, therapeutic interventions, follow-up and outcomes, discussion, patient perspective, and informed consent. Extensions exist for specialty areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARRIVE (animal research)
rubrics_metrics.description: Animal Research: Reporting of In Vivo Experiments (ARRIVE) guidelines for reporting animal studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARRIVE items include study design, experimental procedures, experimental animals, housing and husbandry, sample size, allocation, experimental outcomes, statistical methods, and ethical statement to improve reproducibility and ethical transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: SQUIRE (quality improvement studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for QUality Improvement Reporting Excellence (SQUIRE 2.0) for reporting healthcare improvement work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SQUIRE focuses on context, rationale, intervention description, study of the intervention, measures, analysis, and implications for practice and generalizability in improvement studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHEERS (health economic evaluations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards (CHEERS) – guidance for reporting economic evaluations of health interventions (CHEERS 2022 and AI-related extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHEERS items cover study perspective, comparators, time horizon, discounting, model structure, data sources, analytic methods, outcomes, and uncertainty analyses. Extensions address specific methods (e.g., value of information, AI-related interventions).

rubrics_metrics.name: AGREE and RIGHT (clinical practice guidelines reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: AGREE reporting checklist and RIGHT statement provide standards for reporting clinical practice guidelines and the development process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items cover scope and purpose, stakeholder involvement, rigor of development, clarity of presentation, applicability, editorial independence, and how recommendations were derived and reported (RIGHT includes specific items for introductions and interpretation).

rubrics_metrics.name: COREQ and SRQR (qualitative research)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidated criteria for reporting qualitative research (COREQ) and Standards for Reporting Qualitative Research (SRQR) provide checklists for interviews, focus groups and qualitative methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COREQ (32-item checklist) addresses research team, reflexivity, study design, data collection, analysis, and findings. SRQR gives broader guidance on context, sampling, data collection, analysis, and synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: TIDieR (intervention description and replication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Template for Intervention Description and Replication (TIDieR) checklist to ensure detailed description of interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TIDieR items include name, rationale, materials, procedures, provider, mode of delivery, location, dosage, tailoring, modifications, and fidelity to enable replication and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA-ScR (scoping reviews) and other PRISMA extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of PRISMA tailored to specific review types such as scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR), living systematic reviews, and abstracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each PRISMA extension adapts the main PRISMA items to the particular aims and methods of the review type (e.g., mapping evidence in scoping reviews vs. meta-analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: CLAIM and CLAIM (AI in medical imaging) / SPIRIT-AI / CONSORT-AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklists and extensions aimed at reporting artificial intelligence and machine learning studies in medicine (e.g., CLAIM, SPIRIT-AI, CONSORT-AI, MINIMAR, MI-CLAIM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These guidelines emphasize clear reporting of model development/validation, data sources, preprocessing, reference standards, model performance metrics, explainability, clinical integration, and limitations. Use the AI-specific extension appropriate to study type (protocol, trial, diagnostic, imaging).

rubrics_metrics.name: ARRANGEMENT: Specialty and method-specific guideline entries
rubrics_metrics.description: The Library contains many specialty- and method-specific reporting standards (e.g., STARD-AI, PRISMA-DTA, CONSORT-DEFINE, TIDieR-Rehab, STROBE-MR, RECORD-PE, TRIPOD-Cluster, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For specialized fields (e.g., rehabilitation, dentistry, endodontics, oncology, genomics, imaging, wearable/sensor technologies), select the guideline or extension listed for that specialty to ensure field-relevant reporting items are covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on using reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Library provides links to explanation and elaboration documents, checklists, and development papers to help authors, editors and reviewers apply guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the explanation and elaboration articles, examples of good reporting, and any available translations. The Library also offers 'About the Library' and Help pages that describe scope, inclusion criteria, and how to search for and use guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of protocols, trial design modifications and pandemic/force majeure changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance (e.g., CONSERVE 2021) for reporting trial protocols and completed trials modified due to COVID-19 or other extenuating circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes recommended items to transparently describe deviations, adaptations, and rationale for changes to design, conduct, analysis and reporting during disruptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for reporting harms, adverse events and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple entries and checklists address reporting of harms and adverse events across interventions, pharmacovigilance and device studies (e.g., CONSORT harms items, READUS-PV).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report definitions, ascertainment methods, denominators, timing, severity grading, attribution, withdrawals, and analyses of adverse events per the relevant guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidance for statistical methods, Bayesian analyses, subgroup and heterogeneity reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations and checklists (e.g., SAMBR, Bayesian Analysis Reporting Guidelines, guidance on subgroup analyses) for transparent statistical reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include pre-specified analysis plans, model assumptions, methods for missing data, multiplicity handling, effect estimates with uncertainty, and sensitivity analyses. Use statistical reporting standards relevant to the study design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidance for trials using routinely collected data, registries and real-world evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines such as RECORD, RECORD-PE and CONSORT-ROUTINE address studies using routine health data, registries, or cohort-embedded trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize data provenance, linkage methods, coding definitions, completeness, data quality, and biases particular to routinely collected data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for reporting qualitative methods, mixed methods and participatory research
rubrics_metrics.description: Several checklists and guidance documents (e.g., RATS, ENTREQ, GUIDED, reporting items for mixed methods and participatory approaches) detail how to report qualitative and mixed-methods studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include rationale for methodological choices, sampling and recruitment, data collection instruments, analytic framework, reflexivity, triangulation, and how findings fit with theory and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for reporting interventions and control descriptions (e.g., TIDieR-Placebo, REFLECT, ACURATE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklists to ensure detailed reporting of active interventions and control/sham/placebo procedures so readers can interpret fidelity and mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the intervention/control content, provider training, delivery mode, fidelity checks, adaptations, and any placebo/sham construction and validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for the development and reporting of reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents describing methods for writing trustworthy guidelines and a proposed manuscript template to support guideline development and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the development process (Delphi, consensus), stakeholder involvement, evidence synthesis, piloting, and explain rationale for items included in the guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations and specialty indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Some reporting guidelines are available in languages other than English and the Library indexes translations and specialty-specific adaptations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the Translations section and specialty browse pages to find a guideline in your language or modified for a specific subfield.
